turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mrs Pillay, sit. Sister says two falls. When?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It wasn't really a fall, Doctor. I slid down. Um, Tuesday? Or Monday night? Ag, the days are mixing.

[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tuesday evening, Doc, in the passage by the bedroom. And again yesterday morning in the kitchen. She was flat on the tiles, I had to lift her. She always makes it smaller than it is.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, but I didn't crash down. My legs just went soft and I slid. I was awake the whole time, I promise you.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy when you stand?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, ja. Getting off the bed, or up from the couch. The room goes funny, not spinning exactly, more like I'm going to faint. Is it a stroke? My neighbour in the complex had a stroke last year and she just dropped.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not the stroke story. Chest pain?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you black out? Fully out?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I never lost consciousness. I could hear Naledi the whole time.

[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was grey though, Doc, and she couldn't get a proper sentence out for a few minutes. At the flat she's dizzy every time she stands, not "a bit". She lives alone, I come past after work.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, it's not every single time. Well... it is most times, I suppose. I hold onto the wall now. I'm scared to get up, if I'm honest.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the dizziness been there?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe two weeks? Or longer. I can't put a date on when it started. It just crept in.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not short of breath.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure tablets. Which ones?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine, ten milligrams, in the morning. Enalapril, ten milligrams, morning and night. And for sleep I take zopiclone, seven point five, at bedtime. Must I stop all of them? I'm frightened to just stop, hey.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You're leaving out the water tablet. The hydrochlorothiazide. She stopped that one.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, ja, I stopped the hydrochlorothiazide in March, twenty five milligrams. My ankles were like puddings, so I left it. The chemist renewed the bottle but it's still sitting in the cupboard. I haven't touched it since.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Diabetes tablets? Aspirin? Anything else?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing else. I've had the high blood pressure for years, that's the lot. If you change something, will the pressure shoot straight up? I really don't want a stroke, Doctor.

[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): One tablet, not the lot. Sister's readings: lying, blood pressure one fifty two over eighty six, pulse sixty eight. Standing, one eighteen over seventy, pulse ninety two. A proper drop.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Eish, that's low when I stand, isn't it? So that's why the room goes? Can I still drive to the shops? It's only past the robot, two minutes.

[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Don't drive while you're dizzy. This is your pressure falling when you stand. The tablets are doing too much. I'm cutting the amlodipine from ten milligrams to five, starting tomorrow morning.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the amlodipine? Will five be enough for my pressure? I still take the enalapril twice? And the sleeping tablet, is that the thing making me fall? I've got so many questions, sorry.

[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the enalapril, ten milligrams, morning and night. Keep the zopiclone as it is. Amlodipine five milligrams, once, in the morning, nothing else of it. Stand up slowly. Sit on the edge of the bed first.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it happens at night, when I get up for the loo? Must I phone Naledi? She doesn't stay over, she just checks on me. What if I go down and nobody's there?
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sit down the moment it comes. If you black out, or you get chest pain, go to casualty. No brain scan today.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No scan, are you sure it's not my head? When I stand I can't catch my breath, just for a minute. I said no to that earlier, but actually, ja, I do get breathless. Is that my heart failing?
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Same drop, not a new heart diagnosis from this chair. I'm sending bloods, kidney function and sodium.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Bloods? At this clinic or the lab in town? I'm a proper baby with needles. And when must I come back to you?
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll bring her, Doc. She won't pitch unless I book it. Parking here is a nightmare, hey, I circled the block for ages last Thursday.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clinic lab, this week. I'll see you in two weeks with the results.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, okay. So tomorrow I take the five, not the ten. Do I throw the ten milligram bottle away? I'll mix them up in the dark, I know I will. I'm anxious about that.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Put the ten milligram bottle aside. Don't take it. The pharmacy will give you the five milligrams. One tablet, mornings.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): And the hydrochlorothiazide stays stopped? Even though the ankles were the problem in March and they're fine now? I keep thinking they'll swell up again if I don't take something.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stay off it. Ankles are not swollen today. Two weeks. We're done.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Thank you, Doctor. Naledi, please don't let me forget that lab. I'm still nervous, but I'll try the slow getting-up.

chief_complaint.value: Slid down and dizzy, feeling like going to faint on standing

symptoms.name: could not get a proper sentence out

social_history.description: Lives alone in a flat; family member comes past after work

duration.normalized: stopped in March and not taken since; renewed bottle still in the cupboard

clinical_assessment.assessment: Blood pressure falling on standing because the tablets are doing too much
clinical_assessment.basis: Lying and standing blood pressure drop with dizziness on standing on several blood pressure tablets

procedures_and_investigations.name: kidney function and sodium blood test

clinical_actions.description: Reduce amlodipine from 10 mg to 5 mg once in the morning from tomorrow
Kidney function and sodium blood test at the clinic lab
Do not drive while dizzy
Stand up slowly and sit on the edge of the bed first
Sit down if dizziness comes; go to casualty if she blacks out or gets chest pain
Put the 10 mg amlodipine bottle aside and do not take it
Stay off hydrochlorothiazide
Follow-up consultation
Keep enalapril 10 mg morning and night unchanged
Keep zopiclone 7.5 mg at bedtime unchanged
No brain scan today

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient cannot date when the dizziness began and only says it may have been two weeks or longer.

spec.situation: Older patient who fell twice 'but not really fell, slid down'; dizzy on standing; takes several BP and sleeping tablets; daughter reports what the patient minimises; nurse reads lying and standing BP; doctor changes one tablet.
features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Slid down and dizziness/faint feeling on standing supported; fact says “faint on standing,” not explicitly stated as fainting.
bad.text: Slid down and dizzy and faint on standing (reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient denied shortness of breath when first asked ('No. Not short of breath.') before later correcting herself to say she does get brief breathlessness on standing.
Family member reported that during an episode the patient 'couldn't get a proper sentence out for a few minutes.'
Doctor advised there would be no brain scan today.
Doctor instructed to keep enalapril 10 mg morning and night unchanged.
Doctor instructed to keep zopiclone 7.5 mg at bedtime unchanged.
Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg had been stopped by the patient in March and not taken since, despite a renewed bottle still in the cupboard.
